ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Fracture pattern types: 1

A shaft fracture line crosses the bone nearly perpendicular to its long axis. There is no helical course or separate intermediate segment. Which descriptive pattern best characterizes the orientation of this fracture line?

  1. Transverse fracture
  2. Oblique fracture
  3. Spiral fracture
  4. Comminuted fracture
  5. Segmental fracture
Answer and explanation

Transverse fracture

A transverse fracture runs approximately perpendicular to the long axis.

Option explanations

Transverse fracture: A transverse fracture runs approximately perpendicular to the long axis.

Oblique fracture: An oblique fracture crosses the bone diagonally. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Spiral fracture: A spiral fracture winds around the shaft and commonly reflects torsion. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Comminuted fracture: Comminution produces multiple fragments at the fracture zone. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Segmental fracture: Two distinct fracture levels isolate an intervening bone segment. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
